A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STACI and contain readable methods, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix B.4 report original MSS and AOD benchmark results, qualitative predictions, and ablation experiments.

after.justification: The original benchmark and ablation experiments remain, with revised STACI results and additional GPSat comparisons and CRPS measurements.

M1.justification: The INR dimension expansion, Bayesian Fourier-feature approximation, SVGD training, and local conformal prediction procedure remain unchanged. Alternative bases and non-Gaussian extensions are proposed as future work, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Arctic MSS and March 2025 MODIS AOD data, with the same interpolation, sparse reconstruction, and sampling scenarios. No proposed future application is experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: GPSat is added as an evaluated comparator in both main benchmark tables and the AOD visualization in Figure 2. Deep RF, Deep GP, and SVGP remain; the sampling-ablation comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: CRPS is added as an evaluation metric. The new GPSat comparison uses 1,225 expert locations and reports total fitting time. Appendix B.2 changes the reported STACI-FFNG encoding scale from 1.0 to 5.0 for MSS, retaining 1.0 for AOD. Existing splits, preprocessing, budgets, and ablation grids remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 3 revises the latent-dimension and sampling-fraction results, and Table 3 revises the SVGD-particle ablation. These retain the original analysis questions and tested settings. Figure 2 also extends the qualitative comparison of spatially varying uncertainty to GPSat.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark point estimates without repeated-run error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. SVGD particle counts and predictive uncertainty procedures are retained; revised uncertainty-quality scores do not constitute a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main quantitative record is substantially revised: Tables 1–2 update all STACI Bayesian variants and add GPSat and CRPS results. Under unchanged reported FFNP settings, MSS/AOD RMSE changes from 0.184/0.581 to 0.161/0.560; AOD ResMLP RMSE instead increases from 0.697 to 0.720. GPSat leads AOD NLL and CRPS in v2. Figure 3 changes, and Table 3's decreasing NLL sequence becomes slightly increasing. Conformal scores remain unchanged. The MSS FFNG results accompany a changed reported setting and are not a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: The covariance theorems, Appendix A.1 proof, model equations, and conformal assumptions remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds the standard Gaussian CRPS formula as evaluation documentation, without a new theoretical definition, derivation, or guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims about scalable nonstationary interpolation, interpretable covariance parameters, and valid adaptive prediction intervals. The conclusion's added possibilities are future directions rather than newly achieved contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds GPSat accuracy/runtime tradeoffs and interprets its local GPs as providing spatially adaptive uncertainty. Appendix B.4 replaces the slight NLL-improvement interpretation with approximate stability. The conclusion adds possible data-driven bases, non-Gaussian responses, and point-process extensions while retaining the original limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository pointer, GPSat's expert count and timing convention, dataset-specific FFNG encoding scales, and CRPS calculation details. Existing prior specifications, optimizers, hardware, and most model settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gregory et al. (2024) for GPSat and Lloyd et al. (2015) for GP-modulated Poisson-process extensions. These modestly broaden the comparison and future-work positioning; the remaining cited literature is retained with renumbering.

P1.justification: The section order and most prose remain intact. Local edits correct spelling, update author and acknowledgment information, expand the pipeline caption and AOD explanation, and add future-work and metric descriptions.

P2.justification: The manuscript is retypeset throughout into a compact NeurIPS layout with different typography, spacing, title block, and float placement. Tables 1–2 gain CRPS columns and GPSat rows; Figure 2 gains GPSat panels; Figure 3 changes axis ranges, ticks, and legend styling. Figure 1 retains its graphic with an expanded caption.

improvement.justification: GPSat and CRPS provide a fuller comparison of predictive uncertainty, including results favoring a competitor, while the code/data pointer and additional settings improve reproducibility information. These gains outweigh a localized reporting regression: Section 4.3 still claims that increasing ResMLP's latent dimension from 128 to 256 reduces error, although v2 Figure 3a no longer shows that decrease. Largely unexplained score revisions also limit the improvement.
